intro.heading: A website shouldn't be another thing you have to manage between jobs.
paragraphs: Jobsite Systems is a focused, branded initiative: simple, working websites for trade businesses that need a solid web presence without the ongoing hassle of a traditional WordPress site.

Most owners we talk to have either no website, a DIY site that never quite worked, or a WordPress build that hasn't been updated in years and is now a liability. None of those options bring in estimate requests reliably.

We designed a better middle: a practical, mobile-first trade-business site built on simple, solid hosting — fast, secure, and genuinely low-maintenance. No plugin updates, no security scares the week before busy season.

The package covers everything a homeowner or property manager actually looks for — what you do, where you work, your license and insurance, what work looks like when you're done, and an easy way to request an estimate — and we handle the ongoing care so your site stays online and accurate year after year.

whyStatic.heading: We stopped building on WordPress for a reason.
whyStatic.body: Reformatted into bodyBlocks below — `body` retained as a fallback summary for the editor's text-edit flow.

paragraphs: For most of two decades we shipped sites the way the rest of the industry did — WordPress, plugins, themes, a CMS perched between the trade-business owner and their own pages. It worked, until it didn't.

The calls always landed at the worst time: a plugin update broke the contact form, a security advisory needed triage that morning, the host pushed a PHP version and half the site fell over. The owner hadn't touched anything. The stack had moved out from under them.

Every one of those calls was a reminder that we were charging trade businesses to maintain a problem we'd built for them. A WordPress site isn't really one thing — it's twenty third-party codebases held together with cron jobs and a quarterly maintenance plan.

The longer it runs, the more ways there are for hackers to break in, and the less anyone wants to touch it. Eventually it just sits there looking older every year, until someone has to throw it out and start over.
bodyBlocks.pullQuote: Every plugin is also one more vendor that could touch your customer-facing surface.

paragraphs: A small set of static files. No database, no admin panel, no plugin tray. Served from a CDN that quietly does its job whether anyone is paying attention or not. The first site went live on a Tuesday, and a year later we hadn't touched it. No security patches. No version chasing. Nothing to babysit.

It isn't fancier than WordPress, and it isn't trying to be — it's smaller, simpler, and built around the parts of a website a homeowner actually needs. What you do. Where you work. License and insurance. Real photos of finished work. A way to request an estimate. Everything else was overhead, and we stopped charging trade businesses to carry it.

philosophy.heading: How we build.
philosophy.lede: We build the smallest site that does the job — and we keep it that way. Four ideas guide every decision, in this order.
philosophy.featuredSummary: Homeowners want to know what you do, where you work, and how to reach out.

cards.title: Simple beats clever.
cards.body: We design around those answers — not around trendy patterns that distract from the job. If a section doesn't help a customer decide to pick up the phone, it doesn't belong on the page.

cards.title: Boring is an asset.
cards.body: A website that quietly does its job for three years straight is worth more than one that wows for a week and then needs babysitting. Boring tech runs longer — and for a trade business, boring is the safest posture against a hacked site.

cards.title: Low maintenance, on purpose.
cards.body: No plugins, no admin panel to forget the password to, no PHP upgrades. The site is built once and served fast — updates flow through us, not through a CMS.

cards.title: Direct support.
cards.body: Need a crew member added, a service area changed, or a new before-and-after photo published? One email, handled. No tickets, no account managers.
